items.title: Structural typing
items.body: TypeScript is structurally typed: a value is assignable to a type if it has the required members, regardless of declared names. Two interfaces with identical shapes are interchangeable, and so are two type aliases of string.
items.question: How would you stop code from passing a UserId where an OrderId is expected if both are strings?
items.answer: Use branded types, e.g. type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }, produced only by a validating constructor function. The brand exists only at compile time, so there is no runtime cost.

items.title: Types are erased at runtime
items.body: Type annotations are erased during compilation and TypeScript adds no runtime type checks. Data from JSON.parse, fetch, or environment variables is unchecked; validate it at runtime before treating it as a typed value.

items.title: Prefer unknown over any
items.question: Why prefer unknown over any for values of uncertain type?
items.answer: any turns off checking and spreads silently: anything read from it or assigned from it is unchecked too. unknown accepts any value but forbids using it until you narrow it with typeof, instanceof, in, or a type guard, so the compiler forces the validation step.

items.title: Exhaustive switches with never
items.question: type Shape = Circle | Square, each with a kind field, and many switch statements over shape.kind. Someone adds Triangle. How do you make the compiler flag every switch that forgot it?
items.answer: In each default branch assign the value to a never-typed variable: const unreachable: never = shape. If a case is missing, shape is narrowed to Triangle there, which is not assignable to never, so compilation fails at every incomplete switch.

items.title: as is not a runtime check
items.question: Code does const user = (await res.json()) as User and later crashes on user.profile.name. Why did the compiler not help?
items.answer: as is a type assertion, not a conversion or check: it tells the compiler to trust you, and res.json() returns any anyway. The shape was never verified. Validate with a schema library or a user-defined type guard that returns User only after checking, so bad responses fail at the boundary with a clear error.

items.title: strictNullChecks
items.body: With strictNullChecks (enabled by the strict flag), null and undefined are not assignable to other types, so possibly-missing values must be narrowed before use. Without it, every type silently includes null and undefined.

items.title: Distributive conditional types
items.question: Why does type ToArray<T> = T extends any ? T[] : never turn string | number into string[] | number[] instead of (string | number)[]?
items.answer: Conditional types distribute over unions when the checked type is a naked type parameter: the condition is applied to each member separately and the results are unioned. Wrap both sides in a tuple, [T] extends [any] ? T[] : never, to turn distribution off.

items.title: Enum or string literal union?
items.question: You need a set of string constants for API status values. Choose between a TypeScript enum and a string literal union. What do you weigh?
items.answer: A union like 'active' | 'paused' is fully erased, matches JSON values directly, and works with tools that only strip types. An enum emits a runtime object, and a plain string literal is not assignable to a string enum type. Enums are not erasable syntax, which matters for type-stripping runtimes and the erasableSyntaxOnly compiler option.
